content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment spikes) — model tends to overshoot after sentiment turns positive.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment — model fails to recognize downward momentum when sentiment is consistently negative.
- Exhibit lag in price correction — model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to overprediction followed by sharp drop.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early stages of negative sentiment, underestimating the depth of decline.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: reduce forecast by 5–10% when sentiment is negative and above -0.4, or increase by 5–10% when sentiment is positive and above 0.3.
